world.title: Saudi Arabia Suspends Travel to and from Kenya as Precaution against Ebola
world.description: Saudi Arabia suspended on Friday travel by Saudi citizens to Kenya as part of precautionary measures to mitigate risks associated with the Ebola virus. The measures include halting all visa issuance for individuals arriving from Kenya, and barring entry to travelers arriving directly from Kenya or transiting through third countries if they stayed in Kenya or any other country with an active Ebola outbreak within the 21 days preceding their arrival in the Kingdom.

science.title: TGF-β-induced ganglioside remodeling highlights GD2 as a dynamically regulated target in glioblastoma
science.description: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by extensive cellular plasticity and dynamic interactions with the tumor microenvironment. The tumor-associated ganglioside GD2 is considered a promising therapeutic target, although its stability across different cellular states remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β), a key regulator of glioblastoma progression and mesenchymal reprogramming, modulates ganglioside-biosynthetic gene expression and GD2 surface expression. Using U87-MG and U251-MG glioblastoma cell lines, we combined MALDI–TOF-MS glycosphingolipid profiling, flow cytometry, quantitative PCR, Western blot analysis, and migration assays to characterize TGF-β–induced phenotypic changes. Baseline analyses revealed marked differences in ganglioside composition between the two cell lines. TGF-β induced distinct mesenchymal-like phenotypic responses and differentially regulated ganglioside-biosynthetic gene expression, resulting in opposite effects on GD2 surface expression: GD2 levels increased in U251-MG cells but decreased in U87-MG cells. These changes were accompanied by cell line–specific alterations in migratory behavior. Pharmacological inhibition of UDP-glucose ceramide glucosyltransferase (UGCG) reduced GD2 expression and attenuated migration, supporting a broader contribution of glycosphingolipid biosynthesis to migratory behavior. Together, these findings demonstrate that GD2 expression is dynamically regulated by microenvironmental signaling and is associated with TGF-β-induced phenotypic changes in the glioblastoma cell models examined. Our results identify changes in ganglioside-biosynthetic gene expression and GD2 surface abundance as molecular features accompanying tumor cell plasticity and suggest that GD2 should be considered a context-dependent therapeutic target rather than a stable tumor-associated marker.

science.title: Design of an in-situ CONOSEAL sealing surface repairing equipment for nuclear reactor thermocouple column
science.description: The CONOSEAL seal for the nuclear reactor thermocouple column belongs to the boundary seal of the primary circuit. When the sealing surface suffers from scratches, damages, or other defects, it will directly affect the sealing reliability and result in leakage. However, replacing the thermocouple column is a complex process with huge workload and long period. To address these issues, an in-situ reactor thermocouple column CONOSEAL sealing surface repairing device is designed. Due to the in-situ structure and operation conditions, the repairing device is designed in a compact modular and light weighted manner. Repair tests have been conducted on a thermocouple column to verify the repair capability of the CONOSEAL sealing surface repairing device. A prototype of cycling test platform is established to simulate the in-situ conditions of the thermocouple column. The CONOSEAL sealing surface is repaired to achieve a surface roughness of Ra 1.712 μm and pressure tests according to RCC-M standard and thermal cycling tests are both performed on the thermocouple column. For the pressure tests, the measured pressure drops do not exceed 0.2 MPa during a 10 min pressure maintenance. In the thermal cycling tests, the pressure is maintained for 10 min under the pressure of 15.5 MPa and the temperature is 310 ℃ and there are no leaks. The test results show that the dimensions and roughness of the sealing surface after repairing by the repair device meet the requirements of the in-situ operation conditions. This verifies the capability of the CONOSEAL sealing surface repairing equipment.
